description: An open-source remote desktop application designed for self-hosting, as an alternative to TeamViewer.

summary.one_liner: RustDesk is an open-source, Rust-based remote desktop application that can be self-hosted, positioned as an alternative to TeamViewer.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes RustDesk as a remote desktop solution written in Rust that works without configuration and lets users control their own data. Users can rely on the project's rendezvous/relay server, run their own, or write their own rendezvous/relay server. The desktop GUI is built with Flutter, while the older Sciter UI is marked deprecated. The file structure section lists modules for screen capture (libs/scrap), keyboard and mouse control (libs/enigo), file copy and paste (libs/clipboard), file transfer, and a Flutter codebase for desktop and mobile. The README also covers building from source on Linux, Windows and macOS via cargo and vcpkg, and building through a Docker builder image.
how_to_run: git clone --recurse-submodules <repository URL> (URL not preserved in README)
Install vcpkg and set VCPKG_ROOT; e.g. vcpkg install libvpx libyuv opus aom (Linux/macOS)
Install listed system dependencies for your distribution (e.g. libgtk-3-dev, libxdo-dev, libasound2-dev)
Alternatively: docker build -t "rustdesk-builder" . then run the builder container with the repo mounted
notable: Works out of the box with no configuration required, per the README
Can use the official rendezvous/relay server, self-host one, or write your own
Desktop GUI uses Flutter; the Sciter UI is deprecated
caveats: Sciter UI is deprecated; the Sciter-based build tutorial is described as the easier starting point but the Flutter version is built via CI
Building from source requires vcpkg, C++ toolchain and platform-specific system packages; some distributions need manual libvpx fixes
README includes a misuse disclaimer; authors disclaim responsibility for misuse
